title: Applied ML experiment scratchpad - quant & eval notes (2026-03-04)
content:
Quick notes / working log (personal)

Context:
- Trying to find a quantization + prompt strategy that keeps instr-following and answer quality for the 13B model while reducing memory and per-token cost. Want stable rollouts for Dedicated pools.
- Runs on A100-80GB (dev pool) and local V100 for smaller shots.

TODAY (2026-03-04):
- Ran baseline eval (FP16) and two quant configs (Q4_0 symmetric, Q5_KM mixed) on eval set of 400 prompts (mix of instr-follow / summarization / code).
- Quick perf: FP16 p95 latency (1-token step) ~ 28ms token on A100, Q4_0 ~ 26ms, Q5_KM ~ 30ms (Q5 slightly slower due to de/quant overhead). Memory: FP16 peak 23GB, Q4_0 15.5GB, Q5_KM 12.2GB.

Eval summary (high-level) - automatic metrics:
- Instr-follow BLEU/EM-like proxy (BLEU-ish scoring on reference):
  * FP16: 0.72
  * Q4_0: 0.68
  * Q5_KM: 0.70
- Rouge-L (summaries): FP16 0.61 | Q4_0 0.57 | Q5_KM 0.59
- Code-exec (unit tests on 50 snippets): FP16 pass@1 0.54 | Q4_0 0.46 | Q5_KM 0.51
- Hallucination indicator (factual QA exact match proxy): FP16 0.78 | Q4_0 0.71 | Q5_KM 0.75

Quick impressions:
- Q4_0 is best for memory/cost but has visible drop on code and factual QA. Errors look like token omissions and occasional repetition.
- Q5_KM hits a better quality/cost tradeoff; overhead is OK if we can batch more aggressively. Worth trying a faster dequant kernel to reduce p95.
- For short chat latency-sensitive workloads, Q4_0 might still be acceptable if we use a higher-quality prompt template + prefix caching.

Prompt set notes (used in eval set):
- Instructions: few-shot style with 2 exemplars for code tasks, 1 for summarization, 0 for QA. Need to standardize to either 1 or 2 across to reduce variance.
- Observed sensitivity: Q4_0 produces more terse completions; try adding a length + style constraint in the system prompt (e.g., "expand explanations, avoid single-line code unless requested").

Failures to inspect (examples saved to S3 bucket):
- ID 20260304-codetest-012: Q4_0 produced truncated function body (missing return). FP16 correct.
- ID 20260304-fact-088: Q4_0 hallucinated a citation. Q5_KM partially correct.
(See linked artifacts / S3 folder in confluence doc)

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Re-run Q4_0 with alternative dequant kernel (w/ fused int8 matmul if available) - check PR #412 in serving-runtime (Jordan)
- [ ] Try Q5_KM but enable KV-cache compression (reduce memory for long-context chat)
- [ ] Standardize prompt template and re-evaluate (2 runs: fixed 1-shot vs 2-shot)
- [ ] Add eval metric for repetition rate + token-level perplexity to correlate with human QA failures
- [ ] Get ops estimate for Dedicated pool if we pick Q5_KM (expected throughput delta vs FP16) - follow up with infra (ticket: MLINF-249)

Small experiments to run next (priority order):
1) Q5_KM + batch size 16 + kv-compress = on (run 1000 prompt sample) - check memory/latency and code pass@1.
2) Q4_0 + adjusted system prompt (expand instructions + discourage truncation) - run 400 prompt sample.
3) FP16 baseline but reduce temp / sampling top_k to see if we can match Q5_KM brevity without quant artifacts (sanity check).

Notes on instrumentation:
- Need to capture per-token logits for 50 samples to debug where Q4_0 deviates (save to debug-bucket).
- Add a tracepoint in runtime for quant->fp conversion time to split p95 into kernel vs dequant cost.

Links / refs:
- Confluence: AI-Infra/quant-eval-notes (internal) - contains full run logs and S3 pointers
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/412 (kernel selection change)
- Jira: MLINF-245 (quant eval board), MLINF-249 (ops capacity ask)

Random thoughts / scratch:
- If Q5_KM gives near-FP16 quality on many tasks, we could offer it as a "cost-optimized" model variant for Dedicated (auto-fallback to FP16 for critical routes). Need to think about rollout policy: canary by customer tier + perf regression monitoring.
- Consider adding a small RLHF-style reranker to post-process code completions for correctness signals (cheap filter).

Next actions (today):
- Draft short summary to share on #applied-ml with preliminary numbers (pulling FP16 vs Q5_KM wins/losses). Target: post by EOD PST.
- Kick off Q5_KM batch-16 run (Jordan to help with PR for kernel).

-- Lila
(Notes to self: keep this doc light - transfer cleaned results to Confluence before sync on Monday)
